synopsis: Queensland provides mining-regulator guidance, but QGN 33 covers autonomous mobile machinery in coal mines and explicitly is not a Recognised Standard; the glossary also states that Queensland does not mandate automatic braking [f2129, f2788, f2789, f15525]. Collision risk remains prominent: collisions accounted for 26% of mineral mine and quarry fatalities during 1998–2016, 48 mobile-equipment collisions and near misses were recorded at open-cut coal mines from 1 January to 27 May 2017, and mobile plant collisions topped the reported high-potential incident list in 2024 [f3103, f3106, f3006]. These reports do not establish complete incident frequencies, because near misses are under-reported and that under-reporting distorts frequency estimates [f3049, f3650]. Queensland's illustrative two-second combined operator-reaction and mechanical delay represents 22.2 metres at 40 km/h before braking distance is added, not a measured operator reaction time or validated reaction-time percentile [f3220, f3313, f3475]. Its guidance calls for worst-case stopping assumptions, scenario-by-scenario assessment, and confirmed operator communication for approaching authorized pedestrians [f3403, f3603, f3365]. Validation must also address object discrimination, traffic context, poor visibility, electronic interference and deliberate operator interference; idealised detection zones can create false confidence, while regulator material indicates that false alarms remain an unresolved problem [f3362, f3233, f3375, f3376, f5753, f15551].
